clinician.final_diagnosis: Closed degloving injury of the foot (Morel-Lavallée lesion)
clinician.trajectory_summary: An 18-year-old male presented with foot pain and plantar swelling following a motorcycle crush injury. Initial X-ray was negative for fracture. An MRI of the foot revealed serous fluid collections in both the subcutaneous (~48 cc) and superficial fascial layers (~38 cc), with the deeper collection extending into the phalanxes of the fourth and fifth toes and overlying a stress fracture. Vascular supply and nerve function were intact. The serous collections were managed by incision and drainage with tissue debridement. The patient was discharged upon dermis regeneration and showed good recovery at 1-month and 6-week follow-up, with no recurrence or infection.

The fluid collections were drained via incision and debridement of tissue.
Patient showed good recovery with skin regeneration and no recurrence or infection at follow-up.
